brief: The Russell 2000 has been hit hard by the rates shock, but the setup for a reversal is improving. The index is sitting on major support near its 200-day moving average, the same level where the last undershoot preceded a strong rally. Positioning has been washed out: Goldman's Robert Quinn finds non-dealers bought about $3bn of Russell 2k futures between September 1 and 22, mostly asset managers ($2.2bn), after entering September at a multi-year-low starting point. Small-cap volatility (RVX) has risen only modestly relative to VXN despite the scale of the selloff, showing little panic. The reversal case hinges on rates: the 30-year yield jumped from 5.25% to 5.69% in seven sessions and bond Daily Sentiment collapsed to 10%, leading BTIG, previously positioned for higher yields, to now see rising risk of a sharp tactical reversal lower. BTIG argues this would not necessarily rescue tech; instead it could flip the QQQ/IWM relationship, producing better breadth and stronger small caps while the Mag 7 and QQQ move lower.
